**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reconcile new pushes before finalizing a retried notification**

If `avisarComprobaciones` fails while its snapshot already contains a completed review, and another push arrives before Linear recovers, `driver.advance` retries the pending node with `graph.invoke(null, config)` without incorporating the new head. This conditional then immediately routes to `avisarEstadoFinal` using the old snapshot, potentially announcing “Lista para integrar” even though the driver has already observed a newer, unchecked push. Only the following poll starts tracking that push. Preserve delivery of the pending notice, but reconcile the current head before allowing the retry to generate a subsequent final-state notice.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real: con el aviso de comprobaciones terminadas pendiente, un push nuevo y la revisión ya terminada en la foto, el reintento saltaba al estado final con la foto del push anterior. Arreglado en 0d9e70b: `avisarComprobaciones` va siempre a `esperarRevisor` (como en el diagrama de la decisión 9 del `design.md`), y la foto siguiente decide; si hay push nuevo, vuelve a esperar las comprobaciones. Test de regresión en `driver.test.ts`: «un aviso reintentado tras un push nuevo no da el estado final del push anterior».

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for current checks before finalizing a completed review**

If a required check is rerun on the same SHA while the graph is waiting for the reviewer, or the ruleset adds a required check during that wait, this branch finalizes as soon as the review completes even though the latest snapshot contains pending checks and the timeout has not elapsed. The graph then announces “Necesita intervención” and stops tracking that SHA, so successful completion of those checks never produces the expected “Lista para integrar” notice. Require both the current checks and review to have finished before taking this transition; otherwise keep waiting until completion or timeout.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real: en la espera del revisor, el estado final llegaba en cuanto el revisor terminaba, aunque la foto tuviera una comprobación pendiente (relanzada o recién exigida), y daba «necesita intervención» antes de tiempo. Arreglado en 1cf8413: la espera del revisor termina con la revisión y las comprobaciones de la foto acabadas; si no, sigue esperando hasta el tiempo agotado. Tests de regresión en `tracking.test.ts` y `graph.test.ts` («una comprobación relanzada mientras espera al revisor…»).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the stopped transition when its notification fails**

If Linear rejects the stopped notice, execution throws before recording the PR as stopped or forgetting its active thread. If the maintainer removes the label before a notification succeeds, `advance` resumes the original thread instead of calling `resume`: neither transition notice is retried, and the timeout still includes the entire stopped period. For example, a PR with pending checks stopped during a Linear outage for over 30 minutes immediately reports `needsIntervention` when the label is removed, instead of receiving a fresh 30-minute window. Track the observed stopped transition separately from notification delivery so an outage cannot erase it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, arreglado en 0c7a03a. La transición se apunta en cuanto el driver ve la etiqueta, y los avisos de detenida y reanudada van a una cola por PR que se publica en orden antes y después de avanzarla. Con Linear caído, la PR no avanza, y al volver llegan «Detenida» y «Reanudada» y la espera cuenta desde que se reanuda. Test de regresión con este mismo caso en `driver.test.ts`; el design.md (decisión 3) y D75 lo recogen en 8da96b0.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record the stop before retrying an outstanding graph notice**

If a PR already has a failed `checksFinished` notice when the stop label is observed, and Linear remains unavailable, this retry throws before `stopped.add(number)`. Although the new queue handles rejection of the stopped notice itself, the earlier graph-notice retry still leaves the observed transition unrecorded. If the maintainer removes the label before Linear recovers, `step` continues the original thread rather than calling `resume`: neither transition notice is sent, and the timeout includes the entire stopped period, potentially producing an immediate `needsIntervention` instead of a fresh 30-minute window. Record the observed stop independently of the outstanding graph notice while preserving notification order.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, arreglado en a540d42. La parada se apunta en cuanto el driver ve la etiqueta, antes de reintentar el aviso pendiente del hilo. Terminarla (ese aviso y después encolar «Detenida») se reintenta en cada vuelta, también antes de reanudar si ya le han quitado la etiqueta, así que el orden se mantiene: aviso pendiente, «Detenida», «Reanudada». Test de regresión con este caso en `driver.test.ts`; el design.md (decisión 3) lo recoge en 8feef4d.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record a new stop before flushing pending transition notices**

If Linear rejects a `resumed` notice and the maintainer reapplies `babysitter:stop`, this pre-flush throws before `step` can record the new stop. Unlike the graph-notice cases addressed by the earlier fixes, the new transition-notice queue still blocks observation of the label. If the label remains present for over 30 minutes and is removed before Linear recovers, the driver continues the existing thread without either new transition notice and immediately reports `needsIntervention` for pending checks instead of starting a fresh timeout. Record the observed stop independently of flushing this queue while preserving notification order.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, arreglado en be6bcdc. Es la misma causa que los dos anteriores, así que lo he atacado de raíz: `advance` empieza por `noteStop`, que apunta la parada en cuanto ve la etiqueta sin leer GitHub, avisar ni tocar el grafo. Nada que falle después (la cola, el aviso pendiente del hilo, la foto) puede perderla. Reanudar no se apunta por adelantado: si algo falla, la PR sigue detenida, que es el estado seguro, y la espera cuenta desde que se reanuda de verdad. Test de regresión con este caso en `driver.test.ts`; el design.md (decisión 3) lo recoge en d5348b8.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist the automatically selected strip's ID**

If the panel initially receives strips `[A, B]`, A appears selected but `selectedId` remains `undefined` until the user explicitly selects a strip. Restarting the engine with `[B, A]` therefore selects B, even though A is still declared, contrary to the documented reconnect behavior. Subsequent effect choices then target B rather than the previously selected strip. Store the resolved selection's ID when selecting the initial or fallback strip, while preserving it during disconnection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Hecho en e0db936: `App` guarda el `id` de la tira que se selecciona sola (la primera al abrir, o la primera si falta la elegida), ajustando el estado durante el render. Así, si el motor vuelve con las tiras en otro orden, sigue seleccionada la misma. Sin conexión no hay tiras, y la selección se conserva. Lleva su test con las tiras en orden inverso.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore non-primary pointer buttons when choosing effects**

Right-clicking or middle-clicking an enabled effect button currently calls `choose` and sends a PUT, because `pointerdown` fires for those buttons too. Opening the browser context menu can consequently change the live lighting effect without a normal activation. Filter pointer events to the primary button before choosing the effect, while retaining touch and keyboard activation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Hecho en 16ccb4c: `pointerdown` solo elige con el botón principal (`button` 0, que es también el del dedo y el lápiz). Los botones central y derecho ya no cambian el efecto, y el teclado sigue igual. Lleva un test por cada botón.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for the breathing frame before snapshotting the timeline**

If the effect-state update reaches the page before the next frame tick, both `aria-current` assertions can pass while the timeline still contains no breathing frame. The engine broadcasts the strip-state update synchronously through `strips.watch` (`packages/engine/src/adapters/server.ts:273–275`), whereas frames are broadcast separately by `viewerOutput.write`. Taking a one-time snapshot here can therefore trigger “La tira no ha pintado la respiración” even when the switch completes within 100 ms. Wait for a matching frame before reading the timeline, and continue using its recorded arrival timestamp for the latency assertion.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Hecho en 38b0f77: el test espera, con `expect.poll`, a que llegue un frame de la respiración posterior a la pulsación, y después lee los tiempos. La latencia sigue saliendo del instante de llegada de ese frame. Tres ejecuciones seguidas en verde (27,6, 36,3 y 35,9 ms).

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent pending-notice recovery from requesting a stopped PR review**

If Linear rejects `avisarComprobaciones` and the maintainer adds `babysitter:stop` before the next tick, `driver.ts`'s `finishStopping()` invokes the pending graph to deliver that notice. This new edge then proceeds directly to `pedirRevision`, publishing `@codex review` even though the driver has already observed the stop label. Previously, recovery only finished the pending notification before stopping; it now starts a new external action and consumes a review against the maintainer's stop request. Preserve delivery of the pending notice, but prevent recovery from entering the review-request node once the PR is stopped.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate the current push before recovering a review request**

If Linear rejects the checks-finished notice for push A and push B arrives before recovery, `driver.ts` observes B but resumes the pending graph with `graph.invoke(null, config)`, retaining A's snapshot. After delivering the notice, this node publishes a request marked for A, although `@codex review` reviews the current head B—even if B's checks are pending or failing. The same problem occurs when recovering a failed request. Unlike a push racing with publication, the changed head is already known to the driver here. Preserve pending-notice delivery, but revalidate the current head and its checks before allowing recovery to publish a review request.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, arreglado en f55e8d2: al reintentar un nodo pendiente, si el driver ya ve otro SHA, termina el aviso pero se salta `pedirRevision` (`updateState` como ese nodo) y deja el hilo a la espera del revisor; la foto siguiente lo lleva al push nuevo, que pide la suya al pasar sus comprobaciones. Con el mismo SHA se reintenta como antes. Tres tests en `driver.test.ts`; `design.md` (decisión 6) y README en 38f0872.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Route failed checks directly to the final notification**

When all checks finish with at least one failure and there is no review of the current push, this branch still returns `checksFinished`, sending the graph through `avisarComprobaciones` into `esperarRevisor`. Since `needsReviewRequest` now deliberately prevents requesting a review for failed checks, the PR waits until the timeout for a review that was never requested, then incorrectly reports an unfinished review alongside the check failure. This contradicts the changed failure scenario in `openspec/changes/pr-review-request/specs/pr-tracking/spec.md`: notify the final failure without waiting for review or publishing the checks-finished notice. Route failed checks directly to the final notification and omit the unfinished-review reason when no review was needed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, pero es el alcance de la otra tarea de la historia, MOO-91 (sección 2 de `openspec/changes/pr-review-request/tasks.md`, pasos 2.1-2.4): `afterChecksWait` distingue pasan y fallan, la arista de comprobaciones fallidas va directa a `avisarEstadoFinal` y el estado final sin `reviewSince` no dice que la revisión no ha terminado. El change la planifica como una PR aparte, detrás de esta, y no se mezclan dos tareas en una PR. Hasta entonces no empeora nada respecto a `main`: con una comprobación fallida, la PR ya esperaba una revisión que la *Automatic review* no lanza en los push siguientes y acababa a los 30 min desde el push; sin `reviewSince`, el reloj sigue contando desde el push.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve enough precision for keyboard slider increments**

When the period is near the lower end of its range, rounding each change to two decimal places makes the controlled slider get stuck during keyboard use. For example, at 1 s an ArrowRight step produces `20 ** 0.001 ≈ 1.003`, which rounds back to 1; the next render therefore restores position 0, and subsequent presses cannot advance it. The same problem occurs at 1.5 s and other values below roughly 1.67 s. Preserve the unrounded position/value while interacting, or choose a step and precision that guarantee each keyboard increment changes the controlled value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

El slider ya no redondea el valor: sale tal cual y solo se lee con un decimal, así que cada paso del teclado avanza también cerca de 1 s. Test nuevo en `ControlList.test.tsx` (5c33f37).

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for the successful value echo before discarding the draft**

If the final PUT completes before its WebSocket state message arrives, this subscription discards the released draft while `strip.values` still contains an earlier value. HTTP completion and WebSocket delivery use separate connections, so broadcasting before sending the HTTP response in `server.ts` does not guarantee browser delivery order. The control consequently jumps backward after release and forward again on the echo; starting another adjustment in that interval can also send the stale values back to the engine. On successful requests, retain the draft until the corresponding engine state is observed rather than treating an empty HTTP queue as confirmation; rejected requests should still fall back to engine state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

La cola avisa ahora de qué tira se queda sin envíos y si el motor aplicó el último. Si lo aplicó, el valor local dura hasta que la tira llegue con otros valores (el eco); si no, vuelve al motor. Tests en `use-draft-values.test.ts` (08e6565), D85 actualizada (16825cc).

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invalidate the draft when the active effect changes**

If another panel switches this strip to Energy while a control is being dragged, `ControlList` removes the fields but keeps this hook mounted. The draft remains marked as dragging, and this condition only checks the strip ID, not its effect. Switching back to Breathing therefore displays the old draft indefinitely instead of the defaults restored by `createControl.setEffect`; the next adjustment can also send those stale values back to the engine. Associate drafts with the active effect and invalidate them when it changes, including when switching through an effect without controls.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

El valor local guarda ahora el efecto y se descarta en cuanto el panel ve la tira con otro efecto (o ve otra tira): volver a la respiración muestra los valores por defecto del motor, y el siguiente cambio sale con ellos. Tests en `use-draft-values.test.ts` (7ac144f).

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include request overhead and repeated context in the budget**

When a PR is close to its spending cap, this estimate can admit findings whose actual requests exceed the remaining budget. It counts only the PR context once and the finding objects, whereas `createDecisionModel` adds instructions and criteria for every question and repeats the PR context whenever it splits requests at 32 questions or the context limit. The design's own measurements identify roughly 190 additional tokens per question, so this is particularly significant for short findings or long PR descriptions split across batches. Estimate the complete planned requests, including each batch's context and question overhead, before deciding which findings fit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, arreglado en 8b6ddc7. La estimación pasa al adaptador, el único que sabe cómo son sus peticiones: el puerto `Triager` gana `estimate(context, findings)`, que cuenta el `state` y cada pregunta con sus instrucciones y criterios, y la PR en cada petición si el triaje se parte. `withinBudget` mete por orden los hallazgos cuya estimación, junto con los que ya han entrado, cabe en lo que queda del tope. Tests en `decision-model.test.ts` (la estimación coincide con lo que se manda, en una petición y partida), `triage.test.ts` y `graph.test.ts`; decisión 6 de `design.md` actualizada.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve charged usage when a later batch fails**

If a push requires multiple batches and a later `classifier.invoke` fails, the adapter throws away the `inputTokens` accumulated from successful, already charged batches. The graph catches that exception with its token count still at zero and records no additional spending, allowing subsequent pushes to spend the same budget again and making the cost trace inaccurate. Return partial usage alongside unavailable answers, or propagate it through a structured error that the graph accounts for even when classification fails.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, arreglado en addd7e1. El adaptador lanza ahora `TriageFailedError`, con los tokens que ya ha cobrado, y el nodo `triar` los suma al gasto de la PR; los hallazgos siguen saliendo *exige criterio* y el aviso no cambia. Las peticiones siguen yendo una tras otra a propósito: si falla una, no se paga ninguna más. Tests en `decision-model.test.ts` (falla la segunda petición tras cobrar la primera) y `graph.test.ts` (ese gasto suma).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve accumulated spending when a PR is stopped**

If a PR has already paid for triage on one push, starts tracking another push, and is stopped while waiting, `finishStopping()` in `core/driver.ts` calls `forget()`, which deletes its checkpoint with `checkpointer.deleteThread()`. Resuming creates a fresh state, so this fallback resets the PR's spending to zero and makes the full budget available again without a process restart. Preserve the accumulated spending across stop/resume transitions rather than keeping it exclusively in the disposable tracking checkpoint.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include questions when enforcing the request-size limit**

For batches near the context limit, this calculation excludes the questions, their repeated criteria, and the surrounding request structure, although `request()` sends all of them. Running these helpers with 32 reviewer findings containing 5,430-character explanations produces one batch whose complete request is estimated at 66,166 tokens, exceeding both the 60,000-token guard and the documented 65,536-token context window. This leaves large pushes exposed to provider context-limit errors, which turn the entire triage into `modelUnavailable`. Apply the limit to the complete prospective request, as the budget estimator already does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

nodes.body: Este fichero no debería ser un .test.ts?

No es un `.test.ts` porque no tiene tests propios: los registra cada adaptador, y Vitest fallaría al correrlo solo. Pero sí estaba mal en `src/core`, donde la cobertura y SonarQube lo contaban como código del producto: pasa a `packages/engine/test/` en c45bb89.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check the schema version before changing the database**

When a database from a newer engine version uses a journal mode other than WAL, this statement modifies it before `migrate()` detects the unsupported version. I reproduced this with a database containing migration 99 and `journal_mode=DELETE`: opening the store returned the notice promising not to touch the file, but changed its journal mode to WAL and altered its bytes. The existing test misses this because its fixture already uses WAL. Inspect the migration version without modifying the database before applying journal settings or other initialization writes, so the documented downgrade fallback actually preserves newer state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Corregido en b9cdc65: el adaptador abre solo leyendo, mira si hay migraciones que no conoce y solo después pasa el fichero a WAL y migra. El test reproduce el caso: un fichero en modo `DELETE` con la migración 99 queda igual, byte a byte.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve strip IDs that match prototype property names**

For a strip whose ID is `__proto__`, which `StripConfigSchema` permits as a nonempty string, assigning into this ordinary object invokes the prototype setter instead of creating an own property. A save/load round trip therefore silently loses the strip: saving a state parsed from JSON with that ID succeeds, but `Object.keys(store.load())` is empty. The memory adapter preserves the same input, so the adapters also disagree on the port contract. Build the returned dictionary with a null prototype or `Object.fromEntries()` so every permitted strip ID survives loading.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
Corregido en 3167fea: `load()` monta el estado con `Object.fromEntries`, así un id como `__proto__` queda como propiedad propia. El test va en el contrato y corre contra los dos adaptadores.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Discard the intensity draft after its final echo arrives**

If the last PUT completes before its WebSocket echo arrives, `applied.over` retains the previous engine intensity, and the draft is never discarded after reconciliation. For example, starting at 1, changing to 0.4, releasing, completing the request, and then receiving the 0.4 echo works initially; however, a later engine update back to 1 (through another panel or the API) resurrects the old draft and displays 40% while the lights run at 100%. Retire the draft permanently once the released change has been acknowledged and its final echo received, rather than deciding whether to reuse it by comparing each subsequent engine value with the saved baseline.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Correcto, gracias. Con `useDraftValues` bastaba comparar referencias (cada mensaje `6` trae un objeto nuevo), pero con un número el motor puede volver a la intensidad de antes y el borrador resucitaba. Reproducido con un test en rojo (9d52735) y corregido en fcea4f9: ya aplicado y soltado, el borrador se retira para siempre en cuanto el motor pinta otra intensidad que la de cuando se vació la cola, o ya pinta la del DJ.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for rounded PWM values in the power budget**

For small, valid supplies, summing `v²` underestimates the current represented by the rounded bytes that `encodeAdalight` actually sends. For example, with 173 WS2812B LEDs and a 0.12 A supply, a frame containing 53 channels at 255 and the remaining 466 at 12 is limited to 76 and 12 respectively. `estimateAmps` reports 0.1148 A, but `LED_RESPONSE` maps these values to 23 and 1, corresponding to 0.1322 A—above the declared supply even before idle consumption, when the controller applies no additional brightness cap. The safety tests miss this because they use the same unrounded estimator. Account for the encoded PWM values, including the floor, when checking the final current bound.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real: estimando con `(v/255)²` sin redondear, con 0,12 A, 53 canales a 255 y el resto a 12, se enviaban 132 mA. Arreglado en 838ed32: el límite suma el PWM que se envía (la tabla `LED_RESPONSE`) y, si el frame bajado aún se pasa de la fuente, lo vuelve a bajar sin suelo hasta que cabe. Spec y design en 6312b95; el caso queda como test.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check the minimum supported Node minor version before skipping setup**

If `/usr/bin/node` already contains Node 24.0–24.14, this predicate accepts it and skips the NodeSource installation, even though the root `package.json` requires `>=24.15 <25` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` enables `engineStrict`. The subsequent dependency installation therefore rejects the existing runtime, leaving the instrument uninstalled. Check the full supported version range and upgrade unsupported Node 24 installations instead of accepting every release in the major series.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

@@ -0,0 +1,188 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Instala el instrumento en la Raspberry Pi de la mesa (D110, change `table-install`).
+# Se lanza por SSH, sin clonar antes el repositorio (README §1.4):
+#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/7daysofrain/mood-table-v2/main/deploy/install.sh | sudo bash
+# Con otra rama o etiqueta como argumento (p. ej. la de una PR, para probarla en la mesa):
+#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/7daysofrain/mood-table-v2/<rama>/deploy/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- <rama>
+#
+# Qué hace, en orden (design.md del change, decisión 6):
+#   1. busca una instalación existente y, si la hay, termina sin tocar nada: todavía no sabe
+#      reinstalar (el paso 2, preguntar qué hacer con el fichero de configuración, llega después);
+#   3. instala Node 24 de NodeSource, git y pnpm (corepack), y crea el usuario propio `moodtable`;
+#   4. clona la rama en /opt/moodtable.new, instala las dependencias y construye el panel;
+#   5. deja el fichero de configuración base: la demo, escuchando en todas las interfaces;
+#   6. le da la instalación a `moodtable` y la mueve a /opt/moodtable;
+#   7. registra la unidad de systemd, la arranca y dice la dirección del panel.
+# Todo lo que puede fallar por la red o el disco (3 a 5) pasa antes de tocar /opt/moodtable.
+# -E: la trampa de ERR también salta dentro de las funciones.
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+readonly REPO_URL='https://github.com/7daysofrain/mood-table-v2.git'
+readonly INSTALL_DIR='/opt/moodtable'
+readonly STAGING_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR}.new"
+readonly SERVICE='moodtable'
+readonly SERVICE_USER='moodtable'
+readonly UNIT_PATH="/etc/systemd/system/${SERVICE}.service"
+readonly NODE_MAJOR='24'
+
+# Con `curl … | bash`, la entrada estándar es el propio script: nada de lo que se lanza aquí debe
+# leerla, o se comería el resto. Por eso todo está en funciones y `main` se llama en la última línea.
+
+info() {
+  printf '\n==> %s\n' "$*"
+}
+
+fail() {
+  printf '\nError: %s\n' "$*" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+on_error() {
+  printf '\nLa instalación no ha terminado: falló la línea %s del script (el motivo, justo encima).\n' "$1" >&2
+}
+
+require_root() {
+  if [[ $EUID -ne 0 ]]; then
+    fail 'hay que lanzarlo con sudo: curl -fsSL <url del script> | sudo bash'
+  fi
+}
+
+# Paso 1. La del script está en /opt/moodtable; la anterior de la mesa, en el WorkingDirectory de
+# la unidad registrada (hoy /home/pi/mood-table-v2), sin dar por hecho dónde.
+detect_existing() {
+  if [[ -e $INSTALL_DIR ]]; then
+    printf '%s' "$INSTALL_DIR"
+    return
+  fi
+  if [[ $(systemctl show --property=LoadState --value "${SERVICE}.service") == 'loaded' ]]; then
+    systemctl show --property=WorkingDirectory --value "${SERVICE}.service"
+  fi
+}
+
+refuse_reinstall() {
+  local existing
+  existing=$(detect_existing)
+  if [[ -n $existing ]]; then
+    fail "ya hay una instalación del instrumento en ${existing}. Este script todavía no sabe reinstalar, así que no ha tocado nada."
+  fi
+}
+
+node_is_24() {
+  [[ -x /usr/bin/node ]] && [[ $(/usr/bin/node --version) == "v${NODE_MAJOR}."* ]]

nodes.body: Cierto: con una Node 24 anterior a la 24.15 ya en la Pi, el script se saltaba NodeSource y `pnpm install` la rechazaba después por `engineStrict`. Corregido en c57b3b9: el script exige mayor 24 y menor ≥ 15 (y si no, `apt-get install nodejs` de NodeSource sube a la última 24), y un test (`tooling/install-node-version.test.ts`) vigila que ese rango coincida con `engines.node` del `package.json`.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for external state databases when preserving configuration**

When the existing configuration declares an absolute `instrumentState.path` outside `/opt/moodtable`, choosing `conservar` retains the previous instrument state instead of resetting it as promised. Absolute database paths are explicitly supported by `packages/shared/src/config.ts`; `loadConfig()` preserves them, and `main.ts` opens that database and restores its saved effects and parameters. Not copying `data/` therefore only resets the default storage layout. Handle this supported configuration explicitly, or reject it before changing the installation, rather than reporting that the state starts from zero.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

   " </dev/null)
 }
 
+# Paso 5, al reinstalar. Con conservar, el fichero de la instalación existente pasa tal cual; con
+# sobrescribir, el base, y el anterior se guarda al lado como .bck. data/ (el estado del
+# instrumento) no se copia: empieza de cero.
+write_config() {
+  if [[ $config_choice == 'conservar' ]]; then
+    info "Conservando el fichero de configuración de ${existing_dir}"
+    cp "$(existing_config)" "${STAGING_DIR}/config/local.json"
+    return

nodes.body: Cierto: con `conservar` y un `instrumentState.path` fuera de la instalación (absoluto, o relativo que sale con `../`), el motor nuevo recuperaría el estado, y la spec pide que empiece de cero. Borrar esa base de datos sería tocar algo que no es del script, así que en ba36b30 el script lo rechaza antes de cambiar nada: lo comprueba con el Node de la instalación existente, dice dónde está el estado y propone elegir `sobrescribir` o quitar `instrumentState` del fichero. Una ruta dentro de la instalación sigue valiendo (no se copia, así que empieza de cero). El README §1.4 lo cuenta.
